newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian oil spillage destroys aquatic life.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian oil spillage destroys aquatic life.

text.p: A major oil spillage has been reported at the Tebidaba flowstation in the newly-created Bayelsa state in southeastern Nigeria, the state news agency said on Saturday.
The chairman of the local community's development committee, A.A. Peters told reporters that the spillage had polluted the only source of drinking water in the area and destroyed aquatic life.
According to him the Tebidaba/Brass oil pipeline was the oldest in the area.
Oil spillage is common in Nigeria where mutinational oil companies accuse communities in the oil-producing areas of damaging their pipelines in order to claim compensations.
The communities in turn accuse the companies of failing to replace ageing flowlines and pipelines which tend to cause spillage.
The Nigerian military government said last week it would set up a tribunal for speedy settlement of compensation cases relating to oil spillages.
The tribunal would determine the amount of compensation to be paid for any damage to the environment.
Peters did not say the company involved in the latest spillage but said it should "expedite action to effect payment of compensation to the affected areas."
He said about 20 fishing settlements and towns were affected by the spillage. -- Lagos newsroom + 234 1 263 03 17
